_style: Inventory icon for a hand-drawn point-and-click adventure game. Drawing style exactly like the game art in the references: crisp dark ink outline, watercolor-gouache fill with light paper texture, muted palette, soft shading; no photorealism, no 3D render, no gloss. Icon format like the reference sheet of inventory icons from the previous game in the series: one single object, three-quarter view, centered, filling about 85 percent of the square, isolated on a fully transparent background; no cast shadow, no floor, no frame, no backdrop. ABSOLUTELY NO TEXT: no letters, no numbers, no words, no scribbles. Bold clean silhouette that stays readable when the icon is shown at 56 pixels. The object must look exactly like it does in the first reference image, which is the accepted game art: same shape, colours, materials and details.
ic_plunger: The object: the sink plunger from the reference — a red rubber suction cup and a light varnished wooden handle with a rounded end, a narrow plain yellow sticker band wrapped around the handle (blank, no writing on it). A few white soap-foam flakes cling to the rubber cup and the handle. The plunger lies diagonally, cup at bottom-left, handle rising to the top-right.
ic_menu: The object: the laminated mini-bar menu card from the reference — a cream card sealed in clear plastic lamination with rounded corners, a bright glossy laminate highlight across one corner, a thin grey-green ornamental frame line around the card, a metal grommet hole at the top with a short loop of brown twine. The card face is clean: only a few faint grey horizontal lines, no letters. Slightly tilted, three-quarter view.
ic_map: The object: the guest map of the hotel taken out of the acrylic stand on the reception counter — a clear transparent plastic insert sheet with rounded corners and a faint cool bluish tint, white glare highlights along its edges, one corner slightly curled. On the plastic, a fine blue-ink line drawing of the hotel building exactly as in the right half of the first reference: symmetrical facade with columns, rows of windows and a dome on top; no labels. Slightly tilted, three-quarter view.
ic_key: The object: the old brass key from the reference — a brass key with a round ornate bow and a simple bit, tied with a loop of red thread to a blank cream paper luggage tag with a reinforced eyelet (nothing written on the tag). Key diagonal, tag hanging to the right.
ic_bill: The object: the bill of the underground water clerk from the references — a single sheet of thick moisture-resistant cream paper, slightly curled, with a damp bluish-grey wet edge, faint grey ruled table lines and, on it, a large wet red radiant stamp exactly like the red sun-shaped stamp in the references: a red circle with short rays around it, left by a suction cup, slightly smeared. No letters, no numbers. Three-quarter view, slightly tilted.
ic_token: The object: the brass token from the reference — a plain round worn brass disc with a small punched hole near its edge, slightly tarnished, blank face with no writing. Three-quarter view so the thickness of the disc is visible.
ic_postcard: The object: the Soviet picture postcard from the reference, inside a crinkled clear cellophane sleeve — the picture shows a sunny seaside resort town on a hill above a blue sea, a white border around the picture, no writing anywhere; the cellophane has wrinkles and bright white highlights. Slightly tilted, three-quarter view.
ic_mug: The object: the enamel mug from the reference — a white enamel camp mug with a dark blue rim and a blue-edged handle, the enamel chipped at the rim with small dark rust-brown spots, slightly worn. Three-quarter view, handle to the right.
